topics.title: Vol II: Special Operations & Hazards (206) (Part 1)
topics.sub: Violent incidents, civil unrest, power saws, PPE inspection, tank farms, and police bomb squad and SAU standbys.
concepts: 206.01: Violent incidents use the standard decision model; Fire/EMS never operate inside the inner perimeter (hot zone), only in the warm zone with a coordinated PD plan.
206.01: One strategy per incident: offensive (warm zone entry) or defensive (stay out, receive patients). Law enforcement does not dictate the fire IAP.
206.01: Unforeseen violence: run, hide, fight. Remove yourself, call PD on their tac channel, use the emergency traffic button, fight only as a last resort.
206.01A: Civil unrest: no single-company responses in the geo fence, law enforcement escort, avoid sirens/air horns, fast water/heavy streams, scoop and run.
206.05: Power saws: full PPE and face shield, saws carried with engine stopped, officer supervises cuts above chest height, at least two means of egress.
206.06: PPE inspected at least annually (New/Good/Fair/Exposed/Condemned); turnouts replaced after 10 years; liner wash water max 105 F; Nomex thread.
206.08: Tank Farm: Kinder Morgan shuts down the pipeline via Dispatch; control the spill fire first; never plain water on a floating roof; keep 50% foam in reserve.
206.09 / 206.09A: Bomb squad/SAU standby: nearest ALS company and rescue Code 2, C958 is initial IC and liaison, 1/4-mile premise alert, never inside the inner perimeter.

cards.q: Per M.P. 206.01, PD has set an inner and outer perimeter at a shooting. Where may Fire/EMS crews operate to triage and treat?
cards.a: In the warm zone, between the inner and outer perimeters.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: The area inside the inner perimeter is the Hot Zone and "Fire/EMS resources shall never operate within the inner-perimeter." The warm zone is between the inner and outer perimeters.
opts: In the warm zone, between the inner and outer perimeters
Inside the inner perimeter, as long as PD escorts the crew
Only outside the outer perimeter, in the cold zone
Anywhere inside the inner perimeter once C958 arrives

cards.q: Using the standard risk management plan at a violent incident, how much will we risk for savable property?
cards.a: A little, in a calculated manner.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: The fireground plan applies: risk a lot, in a calculated manner, for savable lives; "risk a little, in a calculated manner, for savable property"; risk nothing for what is already lost.
opts: A little, in a calculated manner
A lot, in a calculated manner
Nothing at all
Whatever PD says is acceptable

cards.q: At a prolonged violent incident where PD cannot ensure safe areas or corridors, what strategy does M.P. 206.01 call for?
cards.a: Defensive: stay outside the hazard zone and receive patients PD removes.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: A defensive strategy is a posture outside the hazard zone, staging or setting up triage, treatment and transport for patients removed from the hot zone. It is used for prolonged or very volatile incidents.
opts: Defensive: stay outside the hazard zone and receive patients PD removes
Offensive under marginal conditions, entering the hot zone for life safety
A mixed strategy: some crews enter while others stage outside
Offensive, entering the inner perimeter behind PD tactical units

cards.q: At a violent incident, who determines the fire department's incident action plan?
cards.a: The fire IC, using information gained from PD.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: "Law enforcement will not dictate a plan of action to our Fire Companies." The IC uses information from PD to set the plan and coordinates it with the PD officers on scene.
opts: The fire IC, using information gained from PD
The senior PD supervisor on scene
C958, who commands all fire units at police incidents
The PD TLO (C958PD) through Alarm

cards.q: Per M.P. 206.01, when should Level II staging be used at a violent incident?
cards.a: For 1st Alarm incidents or greater, or when a defined hazard zone can't be set on arrival.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: Level II staging is for 1st Alarm incidents or greater, or when it is impossible to establish a defined hazard zone when initial companies arrive. Level I is used for single-unit responses with PD.
opts: For 1st Alarm or greater, or when no defined hazard zone can be set
For single-unit responses with PD, whenever the call nature code requires staging
Only after PD has declared the entire scene secure
Only when the incident is within a mile of quarters

cards.q: You're treating a patient in a home when a bystander pulls a knife. Per M.P. 206.01 (run, hide, fight), what is your first priority?
cards.a: Remove yourselves to safety.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: The most effective actions start with "Removing themselves to safety," then calling PD, using cover, and engaging the aggressor "only as an absolute last resort."
opts: Remove yourselves to safety
Talk the person down using your public standing
Overpower the aggressor quickly as a crew
Finish packaging the patient, then leave

cards.q: You're caught in an unpredicted violent situation and it isn't safe to speak. How does M.P. 206.01 say to call for help?
cards.a: Use the emergency traffic button on your portable radio.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: The MP lists "Utilizing the emergency traffic button on our portable radios when it is not safe to speak" among the most effective actions.
opts: Press the emergency traffic button on your portable
Key the fire tactical channel and whisper the location
Have a crew member call 911 on a cell phone to request PD
Send a status message to Alarm from the MCT

cards.q: At a violent incident, what is C958's role?
cards.a: Terrorism Liaison Officer: a 24-hour law enforcement liaison for fire units.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: C958 is the Terrorism Liaison Officer, providing "an on duty, 24-hour law enforcement liaison for fire units" and serving as a technical advisor to the IC, with access to encrypted PD channels.
opts: Terrorism Liaison Officer: 24-hour law enforcement liaison for fire units
Shift Commander who assumes command of all violent incidents
Battalion-level Safety Officer who clears fire crews to enter the inner perimeter
PD tactical medic supervisor who leads warm-zone entries

cards.q: As IC#1 in fast attack at a shooting, you can't get accurate, timely information about the hazard zone. What does M.P. 206.01 say?
cards.a: This may require a change in strategy and removal of all crews from the hazard zone.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01: "Bottom-Line: If the incident commander is unable to get accurate, timely information... this may require a change in strategy and the removal of all fire crews from the hazard zone."
opts: Change strategy and pull all crews from the hazard zone
Continue operations and let sector officers assess conditions
Transfer command to C958 and keep crews working in place
Move crews into the inner perimeter to reach patients faster

cards.q: During civil unrest, Alarm sends a single engine to a dumpster fire inside the geo-fenced area. Per M.P. 206.01A, what's wrong?
cards.a: No single company responses are permitted in the predefined area (geo fence).
cards.why: M.P. 206.01A: "No single company responses will be permitted in the predefined area (geo fence)." All responses are coordinated with law enforcement and include force protection/escort.
opts: No single company responses are permitted in the geo fence
Engines can't respond there without a ladder company
Dumpster fires must be left to burn during unrest
Only a Battalion Chief may respond as a single unit inside the geo fence

cards.q: Responding into an area of civil unrest, what does M.P. 206.01A say about warning devices?
cards.a: Avoid sirens and air horns in the immediate area; lights may be used.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01A: "Use of sirens and air horns should be avoided within the immediate area, lights may be used."
opts: Avoid sirens and air horns; lights may be used
Use sirens and air horns to move the crowd back
Lights off; sirens only at intersections
Run silent and dark the entire response

cards.q: When it is safe to fight a fire during civil unrest, what does M.P. 206.01A emphasize?
cards.a: Fast water with heavy streams, then get out of the area.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01A: Suppression emphasizes "fast water, heavy streams to rapidly control and extinguish the fire and then to get out of the area." Salvage and overhaul may be dropped, handlines limited and roof operations avoided.
opts: Fast water with heavy streams, then get out of the area
Full salvage and overhaul to prevent rekindles
Vertical roof ventilation before the interior attack
Multiple handlines for a coordinated interior attack

cards.q: Per M.P. 206.01A, how are patients best handled at a civil unrest incident?
cards.a: Removed to a treatment area (scoop and run), ideally with law enforcement bringing them to us.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01A: Patients are usually better treated "if removed from the scene to a determined treatment area (scoop and run). A great practice is for law enforcement to bring patients to us."
opts: Scoop and run to a treatment area; ideally PD brings them to us
Treated fully in place so crews don't have to move back through the crowd
Triaged in place by fire crews entering the crowd with escorts
Held until the crowd disperses, then treated where they lie

cards.q: Per M.P. 206.01A, what is added to all responses in known areas of civil unrest?
cards.a: Chief Officers, for additional member safety.
cards.why: M.P. 206.01A: "Chief Officers will be added to all responses to provide for additional member safety in known areas of civil unrest."
opts: Chief Officers, for added member safety
A second ALS rescue on every call
A Haz Mat unit for possible chemical irritants
A ladder company to provide roof lookouts

cards.q: How do you carry the chain saw per M.P. 206.05?
cards.a: Engine stopped, guide bar and chain to the rear, muffler away from your body.
cards.why: M.P. 206.05: "Always carry the chain saw with the engine stopped, the guide bar and saw chain to the rear and the muffler away from your body."
opts: Stopped; bar and chain to the rear; muffler away from body
Idling; bar and chain to the front; muffler away from body
Stopped; bar and chain to the front; muffler away from body
Stopped; bar and chain to the rear; muffler toward body

cards.q: How do you carry the rescue saw per M.P. 206.05?
cards.a: Engine stopped, blade to the front, muffler away from your body.
cards.why: M.P. 206.05: "Carry the rescue saw with the engine stopped, the blade frontward and muffler away from your body." Note the chain saw is the opposite: bar to the rear.
opts: Engine stopped, blade to the front, muffler away from body
Engine stopped, blade to the rear, muffler away from body
Engine idling, blade to the front, muffler away from body
Engine stopped, blade to the front, muffler toward body

cards.q: A power saw cut is needed above chest height. Per M.P. 206.05, this:
cards.a: Is done only under the direct order and/or supervision of an officer.
cards.why: M.P. 206.05: Cutting above chest height is "extremely hazardous" and "shall be conducted only under the direct order and/or under the supervision of an officer," who weighs the value against the hazard.
opts: Is done only under an officer's direct order or supervision
Is acceptable from a ladder if the guide uses the harness
Is prohibited under all circumstances
Is fine as long as the operator's face shield is down

cards.q: Your plan of action before starting a power saw cut should provide for at least how many means of egress, if possible?
cards.a: At least two.
cards.why: M.P. 206.05: The plan should include location and sequence of cuts, wind direction, and "at least two (2) means of egress if possible."
opts: Two
One
Three
Four

cards.q: You spill fuel while refueling a power saw. Per M.P. 206.05, what do you do before starting it?
cards.a: Wipe off the saw.
cards.why: M.P. 206.05: "If fuel is spilled while refueling, wipe off saw before starting." Never refuel with the engine running, and don't restart in a small enclosed space after refueling.
opts: Wipe off the saw
Let the fuel evaporate for 5 minutes
Start it right away to burn off the fuel
Send it in for servicing

cards.q: Why must abrasive rescue saw blades be kept free of petroleum-based products?
cards.a: Petroleum can dissolve the bonding resin, causing the blade to shatter.
cards.why: M.P. 206.05: Contamination "may dissolve the resin which is used to bond the blade, causing the blade to shatter when used." New blades are stored in plastic bags.
opts: It can dissolve the bonding resin so the blade shatters
It dulls the carbide tips so the blade binds and kicks back
Vapors on the blade can ignite from cutting sparks
It makes the blade warp as it heats during cuts

cards.q: When must the rescue saw cutting wheel be examined for nicks or defects?
cards.a: At the beginning of each shift and after each use.
cards.why: M.P. 206.05: "Examine the rescue saw cutting wheel for nicks or defects at the beginning of each shift and after each use."
opts: At the start of each shift and after each use
During the weekly apparatus check and after any blade change
Only after each use
Monthly, during the station equipment inspection

cards.q: Which is one of the five rating categories used in the protective clothing inspection program?
cards.a: Exposed.
cards.why: M.P. 206.06: Items are rated New, Good, Fair, Exposed or Condemned.
opts: Exposed
Serviceable
Retired
Damaged

cards.q: How often are formal protective clothing inspections conducted under M.P. 206.06?
cards.a: At least once a year, during Battalion turnout cleaning.
cards.why: M.P. 206.06: Inspections are conducted "at least one time annually, during Battalion turnout cleaning." Members also check their turnouts every morning.
opts: At least once a year, during Battalion turnout cleaning
Every six months, by Resource Management during a scheduled gear exchange
Once a quarter, by the company officer
Every two years, at Resource Management

cards.q: Per M.P. 206.06, turnout coats and pants are replaced when they are older than:
cards.a: 10 years.
cards.why: M.P. 206.06: Coat and pants are replaced if they no longer fit, don't fit the repair cost matrix, or are "Older than 10 years."
opts: 10 years
5 years
7 years
12 years

cards.q: When washing turnout coat and pant liners, water temperature shall not exceed:
cards.a: 105 degrees F.
cards.why: M.P. 206.06: "Note: water temp shall not exceed 105 degrees F."
opts: 105 degrees F
140 degrees F
120 degrees F
90 degrees F

cards.q: During inspection, a helmet has lost its surface gloss and the surface is flaking. Per M.P. 206.06:
cards.a: Chemical (UV) degradation has occurred; the shell is replaced immediately.
cards.why: M.P. 206.06: Thermoplastics degrade from UV and chemicals; when the helmet loses gloss and flakes, "the shell will be replaced immediately."
opts: It shows degradation; replace the shell immediately
It's cosmetic only; soak it 30 minutes and scrub with a light-duty pad
Rate it Fair and recheck at the next annual inspection
Sand and recoat the shell with approved sealant

cards.q: Repairs to turnouts that require stitching must be made with:
cards.a: Nomex thread.
cards.why: M.P. 206.06: "All repairs requiring stitching must be made with Nomex thread."
opts: Nomex thread
Kevlar-blend thread
Heavy-duty nylon thread
Polyester thread

cards.q: Per M.P. 206.06, what pH range should the mild detergent used on helmets and turnouts have?
cards.why: M.P. 206.06: Use "a mild detergent with a pH level from 6.0 to 10.5" that has been tested for PPE.

cards.q: Major spill at the 51st Ave/Van Buren Tank Farm. How does M.P. 206.08 say the incoming pipeline gets shut down?
cards.a: Command directs Dispatch to contact Kinder Morgan's on-duty operator to shut it down.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: Kinder Morgan has an operator on duty 24 hours who can shut down the flow. "Command should direct the Dispatch Center to contact Kinder Morgan Pipelines." Full stop takes several minutes.
opts: Command has Dispatch contact Kinder Morgan to shut it down
The first-in engine closes the main valve at the manifold
Command asks the facility's responsible party at the Operations Center
A Haz Mat crew closes the inlet valve on the involved tank

cards.q: A tank overflow has ignited: fire in the dike and on the tank surface. Which do you control first?
cards.a: The spill fire, since it will keep re-igniting vapors from the tank.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: "It is always important to control the spill fire before attempting to control the tank surface fire, since a spill fire would continue to re-ignite vapors coming from the tank."
opts: The spill fire, since it keeps re-igniting tank vapors
The tank surface fire, since it is the source
Both at once, with equal foam on each
Exposure tanks first, then let the spill burn off

cards.q: Why does M.P. 206.08 say never to apply plain water onto a floating roof tank?
cards.a: It will probably cause the roof to sink.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: "NEVER apply plain water onto a floating roof--it will probably cause the roof to sink." If the floating roof is lost, the fire can intensify rapidly.
opts: It will probably cause the roof to sink
It will flash to steam and cause a boilover
It will wash away the rubber rim seal
It will cool the tank shell too quickly

cards.q: A floating roof that sits more than how far below the top of the tank shell is a confined space?
cards.a: 5 feet.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: "A floating roof that is more than 5 feet below the top of the tank shell constitutes a confined space," so confined space procedures apply to any entry.
opts: 5 feet
3 feet
10 feet
8 feet

cards.q: A large flammable liquid fire is beyond the foam supply you have on scene. What does M.P. 206.08 direct?
cards.a: Wait for enough foam before attacking; meanwhile hold, protecting exposures.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: Wait until enough foam is on scene before the attack: "If the attack runs out of foam before the fire is controlled, all of the foam will have been wasted." Consider a holding action to protect exposures.
opts: Protect exposures and wait until enough foam is on scene
Start the foam attack now and add foam as it arrives
Apply plain water fog to cool the tank surface first
Use the available foam on the tank surface, then switch to water

cards.q: Fire in an ethanol storage tank. Which is correct per M.P. 206.08?
cards.a: Set the proportioner at 6%; subsurface injection can't be used on polar solvents.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: For ethanol or other polar solvents "the foam proportioner must be set at 6%," and subsurface injection cannot be used because polar solvents absorb the water in the foam.
opts: Set proportioner at 6%; subsurface injection can't be used
Set proportioner at 3%; subsurface injection is preferred
Set proportioner at 1%; use plain water on the floating roof
Set proportioner at 6%; use subsurface injection only

cards.q: After foam solution is pumped into the subsurface injection manifold, how long may it take to reach the burning tank surface?
cards.a: 30 to 60 minutes.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: Depending on line length and tank height, "it may take 30-60 minutes" to reach the burning surface. Velocity over 10 feet/second separates the foam.
opts: 30-60 minutes
5-10 minutes
10-20 minutes
2-3 hours

cards.q: How much of the foam required for extinguishment should the Foam Sector keep available after knockdown?
cards.a: At least 50%.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: "At least 50% of the amount of foam required for extinguishment should be maintained available, especially if tank overhaul is required."
opts: At least 50%
At least 25%
At least 100%
At least 10%

cards.q: Which belongs in the first-arriving unit's initial report at the Tank Farm?
cards.a: Name of the shipper involved and the tank number(s).
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: The initial report includes location/shipper name, type of incident, extent, operation of automatic systems, and tank number(s) and location(s).
opts: Name of the shipper involved and the tank number(s)
Gallons of foam concentrate on hand
Wind speed and the nearest railroad crossing
Name of the Kinder Morgan duty operator

cards.q: Why confirm with tank farm personnel before disconnecting electric power at the Tank Farm?
cards.a: It can close motor-operated valves (blocking subsurface injection), stop transfer pumps and disable controls.
cards.why: M.P. 206.08: Cutting power can shut down transfer pumps at loading racks, "cause motor operated valves on storage tanks to close which prevents subsurface foam injection," and disable tank controls.
opts: It can close tank valves and block subsurface foam injection
It will trip the AFFF deluge systems at every loading rack
It automatically shuts down the incoming pipeline flow
It disables the fixed monitor nozzles used for exposure cooling

cards.q: Once C958 has the target address for a PD bomb squad operation, what premise alert is requested?
cards.a: A minimum 1/4-mile premise alert.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09: C958 requests "a premise alert for a minimum of one/quarter (1/4) of a mile," covering PD evacuation routes and a buffer for secondary devices.
opts: A minimum 1/4-mile radius
A minimum 1/2-mile radius
A minimum one-block radius
A minimum 1,000-foot radius

cards.q: What is dispatched to a Phoenix PD EOD (bomb squad) standby, and how?
cards.a: The nearest ALS fire company and rescue, Code 2 unless C958 requests Code 3.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09: "The nearest ALS fire company and rescue company will be dispatched... Response will be CODE 2 unless Code 3 is requested by C958."
opts: Nearest ALS company and rescue, Code 2 unless C958 requests Code 3
Nearest ALS company and rescue, Code 3 unless C958 requests Code 2
A full first alarm assignment plus a Haz Mat unit, Code 3 to staging
A BLS company only, staged in quarters

cards.q: PD asks your crew to help search a vehicle for a suspected explosive device. Per M.P. 206.09:
cards.a: Decline; fire personnel never search for, handle or remove explosive devices.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09: "At NO time will fire department equipment or personnel become directly involved with a search, handling or removal of an explosive device or material."
opts: Decline; fire crews never search, handle or remove devices
Assist if you are in full PPE and SCBA
Assist only if C958 is present
Assist only after the bomb squad briefing

cards.q: How is fire department communication handled on a police EOD incident?
cards.a: Primarily through C958 on an encrypted channel; units avoid radio talk about the nature or address.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09: For stealth, communications go "primarily through C958 on an encrypted radio channel," and "Units shall avoid any radio traffic in regards to the nature of the incident, address, etc."
opts: Through C958 on an encrypted channel; no radio talk of the address
On the fire tactical channel, using plain language and the address
On the PD tactical channel monitored by all fire units
Through Alarm on the main dispatch channel, using code words

cards.q: If a medical standby at a bomb squad operation runs longer than how long should a company rotation be considered?
cards.a: 2 hours.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09: "If the medical standby is to be of a longer than 2 hours, a rotation of companies should be considered." C958 arranges relief with Dispatch & Deployment.
opts: 2 hours
1 hour
4 hours
6 hours

cards.q: Who acts as the initial Incident Commander for fire resources at a police EOD standby?
cards.a: The C958 Captain (TLO), in unified command with the PD supervisor.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09: "The C958 Captain will act as the initial Incident Commander on scene and will establish a unified command" with PD. A Command Officer takes over fire command if complexity grows.
opts: The C958 Captain (TLO)
The first-arriving company officer
The Deployment Battalion Chief
The PD bomb squad supervisor

cards.q: The bomb squad confirms a mailed USPS package is NOT an explosive. What must C958 ensure next?
cards.a: That radiological/nuclear testing is done and a Field Safe Survey is completed.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09: C958 coordinates with Haz Mat, C957 and the Command Officer "to assure that proper radiological and nuclear testing" is done, ensures the "Field Safe Survey" is completed, and notifies the Public Health Coordinator.
opts: Radiological/nuclear testing and a Field Safe Survey are done
The package is opened on scene by Haz Mat to identify contents
PD takes the package directly to the county crime lab for testing
Fire units clear and the incident is closed

cards.q: Per M.P. 206.09A, what is a law enforcement 'inner perimeter'?
cards.a: A forward, isolated zone where officers in tactical positions engage a hostile or violent suspect.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09A: It is "a forward and isolated zone where law enforcement officers are in tactical positions with protective gear and weapons engaged." No fire personnel, including C958, operate there.
opts: A forward, isolated zone where officers in tactical positions engage the threat
The quarter-mile premise alert zone around the target address
The secured treatment area where SAU officers bring injured patients to fire crews
The area between the police tape and fire staging

cards.q: Responding to an SAU barricade standby, where do fire companies stage?
cards.a: In a safe location outside the police control perimeter and out of the line of possible gunfire.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09A: "Responding companies will stage in a safe location from the scene, outside the Police control perimeter, and out of the line of any possible gun fire."
opts: Outside the police perimeter, out of the line of possible gunfire
Inside the outer perimeter, next to the SAU command post for quick access
At the target address once SAU makes entry
At the nearest fire station, regardless of distance

cards.q: PD requests a CR van at an SAU scene to help families. Per M.P. 206.09A, who must know about it?
cards.a: C958, who is the CR van's point of contact to ensure the scene is secure.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09A: "C958 will be their point of contact to ensure the scene is secure. At no time should CR Van personnel be dispatched to an SAU operation without C958 knowledge."
opts: C958, as their point of contact for scene security
Only the PD SAU supervisor
The Shift Commander, who approves all CR responses
The Rehab unit officer at fire staging

cards.q: An officer is shot in an area at an SAU operation that isn't secure. Per M.P. 206.09A, what happens?
cards.a: Fire won't enter; PD may have to deliver the patient to fire crews at the perimeter.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09A: "Fire personnel WILL NOT enter an area that is not secure... the police department may have to deliver the patients to Fire personnel at the perimeter."
opts: PD may have to bring the patient to fire crews at the perimeter
The closest rescue crew enters behind the SAU shield team to reach the officer
C958 leads a rescue company in under armed escort
The nearest engine crew enters wearing ballistic vests

cards.q: SAU asks to borrow your ladders and TIC for an operation. Per M.P. 206.09A, how is this handled?
cards.a: Case by case; cooperate if appropriate after consulting C958 and the Battalion Chief.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09A: Equipment requests "should be considered on a case by case basis and units will cooperate if the request is appropriate, after consulting with C958 and the Battalion Chief."
opts: Case by case, after consulting C958 and the Battalion Chief
Never; fire equipment may not be loaned to PD
Always, without delay, to support the operation
Only with written approval from the on-duty Shift Commander and Deployment

cards.q: Phoenix PD SAU plans a warrant service outside the Valley-wide Automatic Aid region. Per M.P. 206.09A:
cards.a: PFD units aren't normally sent; local fire/EMS provides care and C958 acts as liaison.
cards.why: M.P. 206.09A: It is "NOT the standard practice" to deploy PFD units outside the Automatic Aid system. C958 contacts local fire/EMS and acts as liaison; initial care comes from the home agency.
opts: Local fire/EMS handles medical; C958 acts as liaison
The nearest PFD ALS company and rescue respond Code 2
C958 responds alone and provides initial treatment
A PFD rescue is sent and stages at the city limits

topics.title: Vol II: Special Operations & Hazards (206) (Part 2)
topics.sub: Youth firesetters, foster care, rescue tools, bee attacks, toxic and bio exposures, pre-plans, CR units, light rail, stalled elevators and MCIs.
concepts: 206.10: Youth firesetters: notify an investigator for intentional fires by ages 8-18; no station tours; counseling is at least seven sessions.
206.11: Emergency foster care: Dispatch contacts DES Protective Services; always advise Phoenix PD, who can usually transport.
206.13: Hydraulic rescue tool: everyone in the area has face shields down; charged 1-1/2" foam line; power unit downwind and away from the injured.
206.14: Bee attacks: ALS engine, ladder and BC Code 3; stop about 150 ft from the colony; three members in full PPE/SCBA; 1 3/4" line on fog; Class A foam only.
206.16 / 206.16A: Toxic exposures go to Dispatch & Deployment and your supervisor right away; asymptomatic bio-exposure victims fill out a card before leaving.
206.18 / 206.20: Pre-plan one tactically significant occupancy each quarter; CR teams auto-dispatch on codes, drownings, 2nd alarms, major assaults, hangings.
206.21: Light rail: OCS 750-950 V DC, 18 ft (14.5 ft at Washington/SR143), stay 10 ft away; derailed LRV, lower the pantograph or de-energize and confirm with a Hot Stick.
206.22 / 206.23: Elevators: Phase 1 recall, then a 30-second power reset; TRT for rooftop hatch. MCI 1 = 2nd alarm + MMRS; MCI 2 adds ALS units at the 3 closest hospitals.

cards.q: A fire was intentionally set by a youth. Per M.P. 206.10, an investigator must be notified if the child is:
cards.a: 8 to 18 years old.
cards.why: M.P. 206.10: "If the fire was set intentionally and the child is 8 to 18 years old an investigator needs to be notified."
opts: 8 to 18 years old
6 to 16 years old
10 to 18 years old
12 to 17 years old

cards.q: A family walks into your station with a child who has been setting fires. What does M.P. 206.10 say NOT to do?
cards.a: Give the child a tour of the station.
cards.why: M.P. 206.10: "TOURS OF THE FIRE STATION ARE INAPPROPRIATE AT THIS TIME," since children may see them as a reward for setting fires. Contact the program (or Alarm if it's a crisis).
opts: Give the child a tour of the fire station
Refer the family to the program office
Contact Alarm if the situation is a crisis
Talk with the parents about fire safety

cards.q: Who must have face shields down during Hydraulic Rescue Tool operations, and why?

Only the operator; flying glass from the vehicle

M.P. 206.08 (01/04) repeats the 'first unit arriving... initial report' heading twice with different bullet lists; cards treat both lists as one report. It also says Command should assign a company to 'assist Foam 44' in the Foam Sector though most foam ops reference Foam 34, and it cites confined space procedures as 'M.P. 204.8'.
M.P. 206.21: OCS is listed as 750-950 V DC while the TPSS output is listed as 650-950 V DC; cards use the OCS figure (750-950).
M.P. 206.06 cites NFPA 1851 2014 Edition; M.P. 206.16A (07/03) is old (bio-exposure card).
M.P. 206.09 and 206.09A are near-duplicates (C958 liaison, 1/4-mile premise alert, Code 2, 2-hour rotation); cards were split so no question repeats across them.
